question: Should OpenClaw core own durable ClawHub publisher-feed trust state and a refresh scheduler, or should this lifecycle live in an external ClawHub/plugin package using a narrow core/SDK seam?
rationale: The patch introduces a new persistent signed-remote-data lifecycle, while repository policy keeps owner-specific integration behavior out of core when existing plugin contracts can carry it; code review cannot safely choose that permanent product boundary.

options.title: Move ownership to a plugin
options.body: Keep core limited to any demonstrably missing generic signed-feed or state seam, and move publisher-specific state, trust configuration, and scheduling into the ClawHub/plugin owner package.

options.title: Approve a bounded core seam
options.body: Explicitly define the generic core contract, trust-key/config ownership, persisted-state lifecycle, and why a plugin cannot own this behavior before narrowing this branch to that contract.

recommendation.title: Move ownership to a plugin
recommendation.body: Keep core limited to any demonstrably missing generic signed-feed or state seam, and move publisher-specific state, trust configuration, and scheduling into the ClawHub/plugin owner package.

likelyOwner.reason: As author of the linked publisher-feed proposal stack, they are the best available routing contact to clarify the proposed ownership and restack after maintainer direction.
